The company, which has 16,154 employees, said it had dismissed 11 people for breaches of its code of conduct relating to discrimination and sexual harassment during the year. It found 13 cases of inappropriate sexual contact, 10 of sexual harassment and one of sexual assault.

item.title: Kerr and Ingebrigtsen to renew 1,500 rivalry next month
item.description: Tokyo Olympics champion Jakob Ingebrigtsen will renew his fierce 1,500m rivalry with Briton Josh Kerr at World Athletics' inaugural Ultimate Championship next month after both athletes received exceptional invitations for the meet.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tokyo Olympics champion Jakob Ingebrigtsen will renew his fierce 1,500m rivalry with Briton Josh Kerr at World Athletics' inaugural Ultimate Championship next month after both athletes received exceptional invitations for the meet. The pair have met multiple times over 1,500m, with Norway's Ingebrigtsen holding a significant head-to-head advantage over Kerr, though they have not faced each other over the distance since the Zurich Diamond League meeting in 2024. Kerr took bronze behind his rival in Tokyo but beat the Norwegian to win gold at the 2023 world championships. The Scot also took silver behind Cole Hocker at the Paris Olympics two years ago, while Ingebrigtsen finished fourth. The pair have traded barbs over the years, with Ingebrigtsen once referring to Kerr as "just the next guy" and boasting he could beat him blindfolded, while Kerr has said the Norwegian has major weaknesses. Ingebrigtsen stoked the rivalry earlier this month when he said he was [USN:L4N44B04J TEXT:"disappointed not to see Kerr"] at the European Championships and that the sport was being ruined by athletes skipping major competitions. Kerr broke the [USN:L4N43K01Y TEXT:"mile world record"] in July at the London Diamond League and followed that up with a [USN:L4N43Z00F TEXT:"gold medal at the Commonwealth Games"] in front of home fans in Glasgow, before skipping the European Championships to manage his workload. "I've made some choices this season that have created plenty of noise, but I've always wanted to prove myself in the biggest races, against the best in the world," Kerr said in a statement on Monday. The stacked 1,500m field at the September 11 to 13 meet in Budapest also includes American Hocker and Portugal's world champion Isaac Nader.

item.title: Kevin Gausman fires 7 sharp innings as Cubs shut out Diamondbacks
item.description: Michael Conforto and Carson Kelly hit back-to-back homers in a three-run sixth, Kevin Gausman threw seven scoreless innings, and the Chicago Cubs beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 7-0 in Phoenix on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Michael Conforto and Carson Kelly hit back-to-back homers in a three-run sixth, Kevin Gausman threw seven scoreless innings, and the Chicago Cubs beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 7-0 in Phoenix on Monday. Conforto, who also doubled and singled, has homered in two straight games and in three of his past eight. The Cubs have 12 homers in the past four games. Gausman (7-11) gave up three hits, all singles, and one walk while striking out six in his fourth start since joining the Cubs at the trade deadline. The D-backs got only one runner past first base off Gausman, when Corbin Carroll walked with one out in the fourth and stole second and third with two outs. Geraldo Perdomo grounded out to end the inning. Ryan Zeferjahn and Caleb Thielbar each threw a scoreless inning to complete Chicago's sixth shutout win of the season. Ian Happ and rookie Pedro Ramirez each had two hits and an RBI for the Cubs, who have won two straight after a three-game losing streak. The Cubs have scored 26 consecutive runs over two games after giving up the first two runs in a 19-2 victory at Seattle on Sunday. Arizona starter Merrill Kelly (8-12) allowed three runs and five hits with four strikeouts and three walks in 5 2/3 innings. He was removed in a 2-0 game after Ramirez's two-out single in the sixth, and Conforto blasted a 431-foot homer to right on reliever Taylor Clarke's second pitch to push the lead to 4-0. Carson Kelly followed with a 392-foot shot to left. The Cubs added two in the seventh. With one out, Michael Busch walked and Alex Bregman singled before Happ hit an RBI double and Nico Hoerner added a sacrifice fly. The D-backs, who had won three of four, managed only five hits, all singles, and were shut out for the ninth time. They are 3-4 without injured second baseman Ketel Marte. Happ singled and scored on Ramirez's triple to open the scoring in the second, and Conforto came home on Seiya Suzuki's double in the fifth to make it 2-0. The Cubs have won all four games against Arizona this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Waiting on Nvidia for next leg of AI rally
item.description: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rae Wee
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rae Wee It's been a [USN:L1N44M00R TEXT:"muted start to the session"] in Asia on Tuesday, with stocks drifting ahead of Nvidia's earnings this week, where expectations are running sky high for the artificial intelligence darling to deliver stellar results. Technology shares remained under pressure following Alibaba's (9988.HK) launch of a [USN:L6N44L021 TEXT:"$10.2 billion share sale"] at a steep discount to fund its AI ambitions as well as disappointment over Samsung Electronics' (005930.KS) [USN:L1N44L00M TEXT:"shareholder-return plan"] in the previous session. Meanwhile, a roughly 45% slump in the [USN:L4N44K01K TEXT:"shares of Unitree"] since a more than fivefold jump on its Shanghai debut has triggered concerns about bubble risk, retail investor losses and flaws in the IPO system. Shares of China's best-known humanoid robot maker were largely flat on Tuesday, following days of declines since its listing. Much now rides on Nvidia to drive the next leg of the AI rally, given its role as a bellwether for the broader AI ecosystem spanning chipmakers and companies financing the rapid expansion of data center capacity. Elsewhere, oil prices were [USN:L4N44L1KV TEXT:"nursing losses"] after threats from the U.S. for an "economic D-Day" of sanctions on Iran turned out to be a damp squib. The U.S. on Monday unveiled an [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"expansion of sanctions"] that it said would cut off Iran's economic lifeline but stopped short of the most punishing measures, instead putting the world on notice to cease doing business with the Islamic Republic. Tehran [USN:L6N44M029 TEXT:"promised to retaliate"] against the sanctions and expressed confidence that major trading partners would resist Washington's pressure campaign. As the war in the Middle East drags on, investors await a string of data releases from Europe this week, including German GDP data and the German Ifo survey later on Tuesday, which could shed light on the economic cost of higher-for-longer energy prices. Key developments that could influence markets on Tuesday: - Germany GDP, Ifo survey - Reopening of 2-year German government debt auction - Reopening of 7-year UK government debt auction - U.S. Conference Board's consumer confidence - Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond President Thomas Barkin speaks

item.title: Rafael Devers' 3-run homer powers Giants past Reds
item.description: Rafael Devers blasted a three-run home run and five relievers took over after injured starter Carson Whisenhunt exited, completing a five-hitter as the San Francisco Giants opened a week-long homestand with a 5-0 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rafael Devers blasted a three-run home run and five relievers took over after injured starter Carson Whisenhunt exited, completing a five-hitter as the San Francisco Giants opened a week-long homestand with a 5-0 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Monday night. Drew Gilbert doubled twice and scored a pair of runs for the Giants, who teed off on Reds ace Chase Burns (14-3) for all five of their runs in the first two innings en route to snapping a four-game losing streak. Whisenhunt stood to benefit from the early offense until experiencing pain in his left forearm while retiring Sal Stewart for the second out of the third inning. After a visit from the trainer at the mound, the left-hander was pulled from the game, having allowed two hits in his 2 2/3 innings. Jason Foley (1-1) recorded the last out of the third, then teamed with fellow relievers Reiver Sanmartin, Ryan Walker, Carson Seymour and Dylan Smith on 6 1/3 innings of three-hit relief. En route to their 10th shutout of the season, the Giants recorded 11 strikeouts in the game, including three by Whisenhunt. The Giants wasted no time getting to Burns, with Gilbert launching his fifth pitch for a ground-rule double and Devers following two pitches later with a single. Jung Hoo Lee drove in the first run with a single, after which Turner Hill plated Devers with a double. Burns retired the first two Giants he faced in the second before Christian Koss singled and Gilbert doubled again, setting the table for Devers, who crushed his 27th home run for a 5-0 lead. Burns was pulled after 3 2/3 innings, having allowed a season-high-tying five runs and a season-high-tying nine hits. He walked one and struck out five. Reds relievers Sam Moll, Julian Garcia and Emilio Pagan combined for 4 1/3 innings of shutout relief. Koss joined Gilbert and Devers with two hits each for the Giants, who lost an earlier series at Cincinnati 2-1. Tyler Stephenson collected two of the Reds' five hits as Cincinnati lost for the third time in four outings on a nine-game trip. The Reds did not record an extra-base hit on a night when they were out-hit 10-5. --Field Level Media

item.title: Austin Hedges, Parker Messick steer streaking Guardians past Angels
item.description: Austin Hedges slammed a two-run homer for the Cleveland Guardians in a 4-2 victory against the Los Angeles Angels on Monday in Anaheim, Calif.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Austin Hedges slammed a two-run homer for the Cleveland Guardians in a 4-2 victory against the Los Angeles Angels on Monday in Anaheim, Calif. Steven Kwan had two hits and scored a run in the opener of the three-game series for the Guardians, who have won five in a row. Cleveland left-hander Parker Messick (10-8) went six innings, allowing one run and three hits while striking out four and walking one. Angels starter George Klassen (2-2) allowed three runs (two earned) and six hits in 5 1/3 innings during his sixth major league start. The rookie right-hander struck out three and walked three. Josh Lowe had two hits for the Angels, who have lost three of four. Cleveland jumped on top in the third inning. Jose Siri made a diving catch in right field to save extra bases on a leadoff drive by Brayan Rocchio, but Kwan and Jose Ramirez followed with line-drive singles. A walk to Jo Adell loaded the bases before Nathaniel Lowe hit a sacrifice fly to deep center, scoring Kwan and ending Klassen's shutout streak at 12 innings. Messick retired the first nine batters in order before Zach Neto lined a single up the middle to start the fourth. Mike Trout then reached out and lined a two-strike pitch up the middle. Neto took third on the play and Trout took second on the throw to third. One out later, Moises Ballesteros dropped a two-strike single into center field, tying the game 1-1. Angels third baseman Denzer Guzman made a two-base error to start the fifth. Klassen nearly got out of the jam, but Adell came up with two outs and grounded a single up the middle to score Rocchio for a 2-1 lead. Klassen came back out for the sixth and gave up a leadoff walk before exiting after retiring the next batter. Blake Weiman got the second out, but Hedges slammed a two-run homer to left-center to extend the lead to 4-1. The Angels put runners on the corners with one out in the ninth off Guardians closer Cade Smith, and Gustavo Campero delivered a sacrifice fly to cut the gap to 4-2. Smith then induced a flyout from Christian Moore to seal his 34th save. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bank stocks put the lie to an Aussie housing crash
item.description: Rate hikes, tax changes, falling mortgage applications and more are raising fears of the biggest home price drop in 40 years. Yet the Big Four lenders like $188 bln Commonwealth Bank trade on healthy multiples. Unless there's a recession, low housing supply will limit the fall.
item.dc:creator: Antony Currie
item.content:encoded: Rate hikes, tax changes, falling mortgage applications and more are raising fears of the biggest home price drop in 40 years. Yet the Big Four lenders like $188 bln Commonwealth Bank trade on healthy multiples. Unless there's a recession, low housing supply will limit the fall. Full view will be published shortly. Follow Antony Currie on Bluesky and LinkedIn .

item.title: ラトニック米商務長官に称賛と非難、米カナダ貿易交渉で土壇場の介入
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米国とカナダの貿易交渉は、ラトニック米商務長官が土壇場でカナダに圧力をかけた後、決裂した。トランプ米大統領は新たな関税を発動し、カナダのカーニー首相は報復を表明している。

両国が本格的な貿易戦争に突入しつつある中、最終局面でラトニック氏が果たした役割に注目が集まっている。同氏は枠組み合意について、カナダに寛大過ぎると判断。譲歩の撤回を求めていた米金属メーカーの代弁者として前面に出た。非公開の交渉内容だとして、事情に詳しい関係者が匿名を条件に語った。

一部の関係者によると、カナダ側はラトニック氏が交渉条件を後から変えたとして非難。一方、米国側の一部企業幹部は、トランプ氏が保護を約束する米金属業界への脅威になりかねない合意を阻止したとして同氏を評価している。

トランプ氏は先週18日、カナダとの通商合意が近いと発表し、幅広いカナダ製品に対する50%の関税発動を延期した。ただ、グリア米通商代表部（USTR）代表が数週間にわたるカナダとの交渉でまとめた枠組みについて、ラトニック氏と関税強硬派のナバロ上級顧問は批判しており、既に対立の構図が生じていた。

ラトニック氏が今回土壇場で介入し、交渉に深く関与したことで、同氏がトランプ政権内でしばしば波乱を引き起こす人物であることが改めて浮き彫りになった。これまでも、米国がさらに優位に立てると判断した通商案件には、積極的に関与してきた。

ラトニック氏は昨年、自動車や鉄鋼への関税を巡る発言をたびたび変え、市場のボラティリティーを高めていた。取りまとめに関与した日本や韓国との合意では、両国が関税軽減と引き換えに数千億ドル規模の投資を約束したが、当初は慎重な受け止めが広がり、その後も合意を巡る疑問が残っている。ただ、大型案件の一部は発表されている。

米当局者は、行き詰まりの責任はカナダ側にあるとしている。ナバロ氏は「USTRは見事な交渉をした。カナダが合意を受け入れなかったのは非常に愚かだった」と指摘。「条件が良くなることはない。カーニー氏はカナダ国民より政治を選んだ」と述べた。

item.title: Reds' Michael Toglia slated for season-ending shoulder surgery
item.description: Cincinnati Reds outfielder/first baseman Michael Toglia will undergo season-ending surgery on Tuesday, four days after injuring his right shoulder while making a diving catch.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cincinnati Reds outfielder/first baseman Michael Toglia will undergo season-ending surgery on Tuesday, four days after injuring his right shoulder while making a diving catch. An MRI on Monday led to a diagnosis of a torn labrum. Reds team doctor Tim Kremchek will perform the operation. The Monday update was a surprise to Toglia, according to Reds manager Terry Francona. "That kid, he swore he was going to play (soon)," Francona said. "When I saw him in the trainer's room the next day, he was trying to do stuff. That's pretty amazing to me." Toglia started in left field against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday, and he laid out to catch Geraldo Perdomo's fly ball in the first inning. He immediately was in pain, flipping the ball away, and he was replaced in the field by TJ Friedl. The Reds placed Toglia on the 10-day injured list on Sunday and promoted utility man Ivan Johnson from Triple-A Louisville. Toglia spent most of the season with Louisville, hitting .273 with 22 homers and 65 RBIs in 97 games before he was called up to the major league club on Aug. 11. In 10 games for the Reds, he hit .115 (3-for-26) with no homers and one RBI. Over the previous four seasons, Toglia played for the Colorado Rockies, and he hit 25 home runs while appearing in 116 games in 2024. In 290 major league games overall, he has a .198 batting average with a .275 on-base percentage, a .384 slugging percentage, 42 homers and 109 RBIs. --Field Level Media

item.title: MLB roundup: Red Sox rally again, top Marlins for 4th straight win
item.description: Anthony Seigler hit a go-ahead RBI triple in the top of the ninth inning as the visiting Boston Red Sox rallied to defeat the Miami Marlins 4-2 on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthony Seigler hit a go-ahead RBI triple in the top of the ninth inning as the visiting Boston Red Sox rallied to defeat the Miami Marlins 4-2 on Monday night. In a game in which "Let's Go Red Sox" chants could be heard into the ninth inning, Aroldis Chapman pitched a scoreless ninth to earn his 30th save. It was the fourth straight win for the Red Sox, who threw out two Marlins runners at the plate -- by first baseman Willson Contreras in the seventh and by reliever Erik Miller in the eighth. Miller (3-0) earned the win. Neither Miami's Sandy Alcantara nor Boston's Ranger Suarez earned a decision, each allowing one run while working around frequent trouble. Alcantara recorded his sixth straight quality start, going seven innings and allowing just six hits. Suarez went five innings, allowing four hits. Rays 4, Tigers 1 Jonathan Aranda drove in two runs, including a solo homer, and Drew Rasmussen pitched six strong innings as Tampa Bay beat host Detroit, handing the Tigers their sixth straight loss. Rasmussen (14-5) won his seventh consecutive start since the All-Star break, limiting the Tigers to one run and three hits while striking out five. Garrett Cleavinger, Manuel Rodriguez and Bryan Baker each tossed an inning of scoreless relief, with Baker recording his 38th save. Chandler Simpson had two hits and drove in a run for the Rays, who extended their lead in the American League East to 3 1/2 games over the idle New York Yankees. Framber Valdez (8-9) gave up all four Tampa Bay runs, three earned, on eight hits in six innings and failed to record a strikeout. Nationals 13, Rockies 3 Daylen Lile had three hits, including a three-run homer, and five RBIs, Cade Cavalli turned in six solid innings and host Washington snapped a four-game losing streak with a rout of Colorado. Jorbit Vivas had three hits and drove in two runs for the Nationals, who had lost eight of nine. Cavalli (12-5) gave up two runs on five hits. He struck out seven and walked one. Cavalli has given up three earned runs or fewer in 14 consecutive starts. Willi Castro and Ezequiel Tovar homered for the Rockies, who have lost seven straight. Rockies starter Ryan Feltner (5-8) gave up seven runs (five earned) on six hits over 5 2/3 innings. He struck out six and walked four. Rangers 11, White Sox 2 Corey Seager went 3-for-4 with three RBIs and Jake Burger and Wyatt Langford each homered while collecting two hits and two RBIs, boosting visiting Texas to a victory against Chicago. Kumar Rocker pitched effectively into the sixth inning as the Rangers romped past the American League Central-leading White Sox to take a half-game lead on the idle Houston Astros atop the AL West. Texas scored in five of its first six times at bat, providing ample support for Rocker, who picked up his first victory since July 27. Rocker (5-10) spaced two runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings. Tristan Peters reached Rocker for a two-run homer in the bottom of the second to pull the White Sox within 3-2. Chicago right-hander Jose Urquidy (2-2) yielded five runs and six hits in three innings with two hit batters. --Field Level Media

item.title: ベッセント財務長官の米長期債買い戻し計画、かつてのメンターが論難
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 著名投資家スタンレー・ドラッケンミラー氏は、ベッセント米財務長官が数十億ドルを投じて米長期債を買い戻す計画を巡り、誤りだと指摘した。ドラッケンミラー氏はヘッジファンドのトレーダーだったベッセント氏をキャリア初期に指導したかつてのメンターだ。

ドラッケンミラー氏は米紙ウォールストリート・ジャーナル（WSJ）への寄稿で、「政府がファンダメンタルズ（経済の基礎的諸条件）に逆らって価格を支えようとしても、必ず失敗する」と指摘した。

ドラッケンミラー氏は「私は50年間、単純な前提に基づいて取引してきた。市場はどの委員会も持たない情報を集約し、価格を通じてその情報を意思決定者に伝える」とコメントした。

その上で「米長期債利回りは世界で最も重要な価格だ。そして、米国に残された唯一の財政規律を促す存在でもある」と論じた

強い調子で書かれたこの寄稿は、ベッセント氏が利回りに影響を及ぼそうとする姿勢に対する反発の大きさを浮き彫りにしている。

長期債買い戻しは元ヘッジファンド運用者のベッセント氏が市場に介入する動きの一例でもある。同氏は最近、米当局による30年ぶりの円買い協調介入を指揮した。米財務省は通貨トレーダーに影響を与えるため、市場参加者に相場水準を確認する「レートチェック」も実施した。

米財務省が短期国債の発行を増やすことで長期金利を直接押し下げようとする試みは、米連邦準備制度が市場の混乱時に用いた「ツイストオペ」を想起させる。しかし、通常は財政安定の番人と見なされる米財務省が、こうした債券市場の管理に乗り出すことは、その役割を逸脱しているとして債券投資家は警戒感を抱いている。

ドラッケンミラー氏は、米財務省が債券市場に影響を与えようとすること自体が誤りであるだけでなく、現在の状況を踏まえれば合理性もないと主張。米10年債利回りは経済の名目成長率とほぼ同水準にあり、金融環境は引き締め的ではなく緩和的だと指摘した。

item.title: India wanted red flags on chip packets and soda. Big Food fought back.
item.description: A can of Fanta sold in London has 63 calories. Buy the same brand in India, and it contains three times as much sugar. It also includes artificial dye, whose presence in food products in Europe requires a prominent health warning.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Kalra, Richa Naidu
item.content:encoded: A can of Fanta sold in London has 63 calories. Buy the same brand in India, and it contains three times as much sugar. It also includes artificial dye, whose presence in food products in Europe requires a prominent health warning. In India, the colorant’s presence is noted merely in small print on the back of the can. That suits some of the world’s biggest companies, which have [USN:KBN16N0UE TEXT:"long resisted"] Indian efforts to mandate nutritional warnings on the front of packaged products. Consumer giants like Coca-Cola, which makes Fanta, appear to have the advantage. India’s food-safety regulator said in August that it had abandoned a push for colorful warnings on the front of food packaging. It said such warning labels don't account for how Indian cuisine has more intense flavors than Western food and instead proposed that companies display a black-and-white table of sugar, fat and salt content. India's Supreme Court is scrutinizing that decision after a petition by public health activists. At stake are the waistlines of the 450 million Indians who could be obese or overweight by 2050, according to a recent study published in the journal Lancet. Experts say more transparency in labeling can forge healthier eating habits. At their urging, roughly 20 nations have adopted interpretive labels — which may include highlighting high sugar levels in red and low fat content in green — on the front of packaged foods. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India buckled after a tense March meeting with industry executives, who argued that such warning labels were confusing and ineffective, according to recordings reviewed by Reuters. Executives also urged regulators to focus on encouraging portion control. Details of the meeting are reported by Reuters for the first time. It is “very simplistic” to believe that a consumer who doesn’t already read ingredient lists “will be so informed by seeing a symbol or an icon on the label” that their diet significantly improves, senior Coca-Cola India executive Mili Bhattacharya said at the March 19 meeting. She added that warning labels were pointless because they would not prevent consumers from otherwise having sugary and salty foods. And they were unnecessary because Indian doctors had done a good job teaching their patients what food should be avoided. Coca-Cola and its bottling partners, however, have voluntarily added traffic-light-style labels to their drinks in some two dozen European markets. Such labels provide “clear and transparent” information, Coca-Cola HBC, a Switzerland-based affiliate, says on its website. Nestle is a member of Indian lobbies that fought the regulator’s erstwhile proposals. But the company has voluntarily used interpretive labels in Britain since 2013. Coca-Cola and Nestle declined to comment for this article. For this report, Reuters reviewed the audio recordings, hundreds of pages of government and corporate documents, and interviewed 11 industry executives and health experts. Several food companies have filed legal complaints against social-media influencers who have criticized how they market their products in India. The threat that warning labels pose to profits means the industry is incentivized “to hold out for as long as possible, not informing the Indian public about the healthiness of the foods that they're selling," said Simone Pettigrew, head of food policy at the George Institute for Global Health in Australia. Lobbying by interest groups has “almost paralyzed” regulators from enacting tougher standards, said Pettigrew, who has researched front-of-pack labels in more than two dozen countries. The FSSAI declined to comment, citing ongoing court proceedings involving labeling policy. MAKE INDIA HEALTHY (AGAIN)? Nearly 80% of products made by India’s over $100 billion packaged food and beverages market could be regarded as high in fat, sugar and salt, according to industry estimates. That means packaging would be awash in red if the industry adopted color-coded warning labels, Deepak Jolly of the Ind Food & Beverage Association said at the March meeting with regulators. IFBA, which represents companies including PepsiCo, said in response to Reuters questions that it wants more clarity from regulators. Current proposals, it said, might lead to "high sugar" warning labels on coconut water packs that contain only natural sugar. Indian regulators since 2017 have floated proposals such as prominent color-coded warnings and star ratings that indicate a product’s nutritional value. But producers are required only to list ingredients and basic nutritional information on the back of packaging. Health activists seeking greater transparency have petitioned the Supreme Court, which in February directed regulators to consider warning labels. It suggested that the agency examine Israel’s system of red-and-green messaging. After the March meeting with industry, however, the FSSAI backed off on interpretive labeling. It told the court in August that it was “difficult” to match international standards on packaging, echoing the industry position. That earned it a rebuke from judges, who said “the world should know that India is very much concerned about the overall health of its citizens.” As India grows more affluent, middle-class consumers have also become more conscious of their health. Monthly sales of [USN:L4N40K11E TEXT:"weight-loss drugs that reduce appetites"] have grown 400% since early 2025, according to market-research firm Pharmarack. Revant Himatsingka, also known as FoodPharmer, speaks during an interview at his office in Mumbai. REUTERS/Francis Mascarenhas On social media, activists and influencers are campaigning against processed and packaged food. Among them is Revant Himatsingka. The former McKinsey management consultant has built an audience of more than 5 million across YouTube and Instagram, where the 34-year-old goes by the name Food Pharmer. The videos have occasionally landed him in hot water. In 2023, Himatsingka made a clip that criticized the amount of sugar and artificial sweetener used in PepsiCo's Sting caffeine drink. The beverage, marketed as an energy drink, is popular with young people in India. PepsiCo successfully sought a take-down order from a Delhi court. It argued that the claims made in the video were false and intended to instigate a campaign against the beverage. Indian regulators in July ordered PepsiCo and other companies to drop the “energy drink” label in [USN:L4N43Q11M TEXT:"90 days"]. PepsiCo did not respond to questions. The bottle of Fanta soda retailed in India, left, contains artificial dye that is not present in the similarly-branded product sold in Britain. TALE OF TWO RECIPES Multinational food producers often make different versions of the same products to comply with local regulations, tastes and spending capacity. Mexican Coke, for instance, has achieved cult status due to its less-syrupy taste. “Pricing and affordability are one of the biggest reasons recipes differ so much across countries," said former Mondelez executive Parul Sharma. But in India, many consumers feel that they are being sold inferior products, said Himatsingka, who has made videos that unfavorably compare the ingredients in the Indian version of Fanta and Nestle’s KitKat against those sold in Europe and Australia. Indian standard KitKats have 4.5% cocoa solids, while the milk chocolate in the Australian version contains at least 22% cocoa. All variants of Nestle’s Maggi instant noodles sold in India are made with palm oil, whereas many versions sold in Britain use pricier sunflower oil. Many of the Maggi packets sold in Britain are made in India, but they carry red front-of-pack labels warning of their high salt content. “It is the frustration of feeling cheated," Himatsingka said. There are some signs that changing consumer tastes are forcing companies to evolve. Nestle in 2024, for instance, announced it would start selling sugar-free Cerelac baby food in India. Activists, including Himatsingka, had complained that for 50 years, only the version that contained sugar was sold in the country. The company has long sold sugar-free Cerelac elsewhere. Nestle's Maggi Masala 2-Minute Noodles sold in Britain, right, feature color-coded front-of-pack labels that are not present in the version retailed in India.

item.title: Australian developer Bathla calls in administrators, citing 'perfect storm'
item.description: Bathla Group, an Australian residential property developer, called in external administrators to help restructure itself as it navigates a "perfect storm" of softening sales, rising costs and tax changes aimed at improving affordability.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bathla Group, an Australian residential property developer, called in external administrators to help restructure itself as it navigates a "perfect storm" of softening sales, rising costs and tax changes aimed at improving affordability. The privately owned employer of 226 people had A$3.2 billion ($2.29 billion) in liabilities as of June 2025, regulatory filings show. The company hired restructuring firm Teneo to ensure it can continue supplying housing in Sydney, its main market, and elsewhere, according to its website. Bathla's move comes amid turmoil in the [USN:L4N43N210 TEXT:"Australian housing market"], which has seen sale prices and volumes decline through 2026. The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has driven up materials costs and interest rates, and the government [USN:L6N41Q05K TEXT:"cut tax concessions"] for investment properties in its May budget. It also presents a blow to a federal government goal to have 1.2 million homes [USN:L4N43W383 TEXT:"built by 2030"] to address a housing shortage. Bathla currently has thousands of homes under construction, according to media reports. "A perfect storm of circumstances ... contributed to the group's circumstances," the company's website said. The causes included "a significant softening in sales, impacts from the changes made in the Federal Government's May Budget and falling confidence in key markets," the company said. The changing market conditions "coincided with significant increases in construction costs which have been absorbed by the group," it added. The administrators' immediate priority is to stabilise the group's operations and work with lenders and other key stakeholders to support employees and the continued delivery of projects, Teneo said in a statement. Established in 1997, Bathla says it develops budget-friendly housing estates, townhouses and apartments in the states of New South Wales, South Australia and Victoria. Last month, ASX-listed investment manager Centuria Capital Group (CNI.AX) said it loaned A$4.5 million to a subsidiary of Bathla Group. According to Australian media, Bathla's lenders include PAG Asia Capital, CVS Lane Capital Partners, Balmain, Ray White Capital, Keyview, Credit Connect in Queensland and La Trobe Financial. Representatives of the reported creditors did not immediately respond to requests for comment. ($1 = 1.3982 Australian dollars)

item.title: Indian central bank likely intervenes to keep lid on rupee weakness, traders say
item.description: The Indian central bank likely intervened in the foreign exchange market on Tuesday, four traders told Reuters on Tuesday, to shield the currency against pressure on account of elevated oil prices and sustained corporate dollar demand.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Indian central bank likely intervened in the foreign exchange market on Tuesday, four traders told Reuters on Tuesday, to shield the currency against pressure on account of elevated oil prices and sustained corporate dollar demand. The rupee was little changed on the day at 95.7350 per dollar, clinging to an under 1-paisa trading range as interventions continued to sap volatility. State-run banks were spotted offering dollars, most likely on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India, traders said. Sustained interventions over recent trading sessions have kept the rupee anchored in a tight band despite volatility in global markets.

item.title: 欧州美術品盗難、換金性重視で金や宝石狙った事件が増加
item.description:
Julia Payne
[ブリュッセル ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Julia Payne

[ブリュッセル ２４日 ロイター] - 欧州刑事警察機構（ユーロポール）は２４日、欧州で発生する美術品盗難について、絵画などよりも換金性が高い金や宝石を狙った、より暴力的な強盗事件が増加しているとの報告書を公表した。従来の専門的な窃盗団に代わり、交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）を通じて実行役が集められた場当たり的な犯罪グループが関与するケースも増えていると指摘した。

報告書によると、昨年１０月にパリのルーブル美術館で発生した事件はこうした傾向を象徴する事例だ。犯人らは警備員や来館者を脅迫し、ウジェニー皇后のティアラなど総額８８００万ユーロ（約１６３億５０００万円）相当の宝飾品を盗んだとされる。

ユーロポールは、この２年間で美術品窃盗犯の標的が、より高い利益を得やすい貴金属や宝石、文化財へと移行していると分析した。

金価格は過去２年間で８５％上昇している。ロンドン地金市場協会（ＬＢＭＡ）は「金価格が歴史的な高値水準に上昇する中で、不正な資金流入や市場のゆがみも拡大している」と警告する。

報告書は「貴金属は溶解すれば痕跡が残りにくく、不正流通が容易になる。宝飾品に使われた宝石も取り外して転売しやすい」と指摘した。

item.title: Taiwan Floods Kill One, Disrupt Flights as More Rain Predicted
item.description: Torrential rain in Taiwan has killed one person and injured at least 164 people, with authorities bracing for more bad weather as Typhoon Saudel approaches.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- Torrential rain in Taiwan has killed one person and injured at least 164 people, with authorities bracing for more bad weather as Typhoon Saudel approaches.Rescuers are searching for four people missing due to heavy rains, which have mostly affected central, southern and eastern Taiwan. Landslides and road damage having disrupted travel and forced the evacuation of more than 6,100 people from high-risk areas, mainly in Kaohsiung, Pingtung and Hualien, where some districts have suspended work and classes.The southern city of Kaohsiung recorded 913mm — roughly three feet — of rainfall in just three days, shattering both 24-hour and three-day accumulated rainfall records, the city government said in a Facebook post. There have been no major disruptions to industrial production on the island, where Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. produces some of the world’s most advanced chips. TSMC said Monday that it has completed routine heavy rain protection procedures and all wafer fabs are operating normally.Still, several airlines have amended flight plans to Okinawa due to the approach of Typhoon Saudel, even as the storm is not expected to make landfall in Taiwan. Advisories warning of very heavy rain remain in force for much of the island. Authorities said flooding has been reported in 35 locations in Taiwan, with 21,071 households experiencing power outages. Taiwan Railway Corp. announced that all express trains on the Eastern Line and South Link Line would resume normal operations after being suspended on Monday.--With assistance from Debby Wu.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Thailand car production rises 6.1% on year in July
item.description: Car production in Thailand rose 6.12% in July from a year earlier to 117,383 units, the Federation of Thai Industries said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Car production in Thailand rose 6.12% in July from a year earlier to 117,383 units, the Federation of Thai Industries said on Tuesday. The reading follows a year-on-year [USN:L6N43Q08Q TEXT:"fall of 7.55% in June"]. The FTI has previously forecast a 3.33% drop in car production for the whole of 2026. July domestic car sales rose 20.07% versus a rise of 17.26% in June, the federation said. Exports in July rose 2.39% compared to a drop of 7.45% in the previous month, according to the FTI. Thailand is Southeast Asia's biggest auto production centre and an export base for some of the world's leading carmakers, including Toyota (7203.T) and Honda (7267.T) .

item.title: United States sanctions oil trader Wellbred over Iran links
item.description: The United States imposed sanctions on Singapore-based Wellbred Capital and its trading firms in the United Arab Emirates and Switzerland, citing links with Iran, as it steps up measures to target Tehran's global financial links.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States imposed sanctions on Singapore-based Wellbred Capital and its trading firms in the United Arab Emirates and Switzerland, citing links with Iran, as it steps up [USN:L1N44L0FC TEXT:"measures"] to target Tehran's global financial links. The company had ties to Iranian oil shipping magnate Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani, the U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control said on its website on Monday. "Shamkhani built Wellbred as a company outside the network’s Iranian business, though Shamkhani is ultimately responsible for Wellbred’s operations," it added in a statement outlining the measures targeting nearly 60 companies, individuals and ships. Wellbred did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Also sanctioned were Dubai-based Wellbred Trading FZCO, Wellbred Trading SA in Geneva and its French biofuels refinery La Nivernaise de Raffinage SAS. With headquarters in Singapore, Wellbred trades in oil, naphtha, petrochemicals and liquefied petroleum gas and has offices in the United Arab Emirates, Switzerland, Saudi Arabia and Nigeria, it says on its website. OFAC had previously designated individuals, entities and vessels forming part of a vast shipping empire controlled by Shamkhani in July 2025 and April 2026. Shamkhani, the son of now-deceased senior Iranian security official Ali Shamkhani, operates a massive fleet of tankers and containerships, OFAC had said. The network ferries oil and petroleum products from Iran and Russia, as well as other cargo, to buyers around the world, generating profits running into tens of billions of dollars, OFAC added.

item.title: Pakistan and Iran made 'significant progress' in talks on conflict, minister says
item.description: Pakistan and Iran made "significant progress" in talks that focused on the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and a path to peace, Pakistan's interior minister said on Tuesday, at the end of a visit to Tehran.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pakistan and Iran made "significant progress" in talks that focused on the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and a path to peace, Pakistan's interior minister said on Tuesday, at the end of a visit to Tehran. Talks between the two sides focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an expedited termination of the conflict, a statement from the Pakistani military said about the meeting between the country's army chief, Asim Munir, and the Iranian leadership. The two sides also exchanged views on regional peace and the way to arrive at a negotiated settlement to the dispute, the statement said. "The Iranian President candidly shared his government's perspective and we had a very constructive exchange on the issues involved," Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who accompanied Munir to Tehran, said in a post on X. The White House and the State Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment made outside business hours. Munir [USN:L1N44L090 TEXT:"spoke with U.S. President"] Donald Trump ahead of his Tehran visit, Reuters reported on Monday. Trump last week warned of [USN:L6N44H0PZ TEXT:"economic consequences"] against any country that provided "any type of lifeline to Iran" as he seeks to isolate the country. Iran in turn vowed to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf.

item.title: Japan plans no crude oil release from national reserve in September, October
item.description: Japan plans no additional releases of crude oil from its national reserves in September or October, Economy, Trade and Industry Minister Ryosei Akazawa said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan plans no additional releases of crude oil from its national reserves in September or October, Economy, Trade and Industry Minister Ryosei Akazawa said on Tuesday. Crude oil procurement in September is expected to fall to about 80% of last year's average monthly volume from 100% in August, as tankers that would normally transit the Bab el-Mandeb Strait are being rerouted via the longer Suez route, he said. Japan expects August procurement to match last year's monthly average, but September volumes will decline because shipments via the Suez route take about 55 days to reach Japan, compared with 21 to 23 days via the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Akazawa told a press conference. "Of the national reserves for which a release has already been decided, there remains a portion that has not been utilised due to progress in securing alternative supplies. Using that portion would ensure (September) crude oil supply equivalent to an average month last year," Akazawa said. Japan expects crude oil procurement to return to last year's average monthly level in October, he added.

item.title: Apple set to launch its new Mac mini, first upgrade in nearly two years
item.description: The upgrade follows a surge in demand for the current Mac mini, which has become a popular tool for running artificial intelligence applications locally ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Mark Gurman Apple Inc. is gearing up to launch a new version of its Mac mini desktop computer for the first time in almost two years, according to people familiar with the matter. The new desktop will debut as soon as the coming days, potentially putting the unveiling ahead of a September event to introduce the next iPhones, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the plan isn’t public. Apple has tested versions with both the M5 and M6 generations of its processor line.  The upgrade follows a surge in demand for the current Mac mini, which has become a popular tool for running artificial intelligence applications locally. At the same time, memory-chip shortages have made it harder for Apple to keep the product in stock.  A spokesperson for Cupertino, California-based Apple declined to comment.  The updated machine is part of a wave of new products coming in the second half of this year. Later this week, Apple is poised to send out invitations for its iPhone launch presentation. That event, which is likely to be held on Sept. 9, will introduce the company’s first foldable smartphone, as well as the iPhone 18 Pro line.  The company is also preparing a range of new Apple Watches with minor changes, including upgrades to fitness tracking and a ceramic-case option for Series 12 models. And it’s planning to debut fresh AirPods as early as the September product launch event. The rollout will include new AirPods 5, an update to Apple’s entry-level earbuds, the people said. That model was last refreshed in 2024. A camera-equipped version of the AirPods, meanwhile, isn’t expected until next year. Apple is also on track to debut its first-ever smart home device with a screen this year. The product will rely on facial recognition to identify users and display personalized content. The company is readying a new Apple TV set-top box and HomePod mini smart speaker as well.  Other new products this year include a revamped iPad mini with an OLED screen. That technology, short for organic light-emitting diode, offers a crisper picture than the tablet had before and brings it closer in line with more premium iPads. The new model is due to arrive by the end of October. Additional Macs are coming as well, though they are likely to be further out. That includes an iMac with new color options, as well as a refreshed entry-level MacBook Pro. They will use M6 chips, the upcoming generation. The most significant Mac introduction in the pipeline will be Apple’s first touch-screen computer. The company will add that capability to new MacBook Pro models, in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, that will also include redesigned cases and OLED screens.  The Mac mini will likely be the last new product to launch under the watch of Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook, who is handing the reins to John Ternus on Sept. 1. Ternus will oversee the rollout of the foldable iPhone and the other major new products in the company’s pipeline.  Looking ahead to 2027, Apple is planning updates to the entry-level iPad and iPad Air; new MacBook Air and MacBook Neo models; second-generation versions of the touch MacBooks that use chips from the upcoming M7 series; a second-generation foldable iPhone; and an iPhone with curved glass to mark the device’s 20-year anniversary.  It’s also planning a push into AI wearables, starting with the AirPods with cameras. As part of that effort, the company aims to introduce smart glasses that would put it in competition with Meta Platforms Inc. And it’s been testing a pendant with cameras that can feed visual data into iPhones for AI processing. The Mac mini has been a particular pain point for Apple’s supply chain in recent months, with deliveries to customers taking weeks or months to be completed. Cook said the problem would take a while to resolve, and it’s unclear how the new model will affect wait times.  The computer is also central to Apple’s pledge to bring more manufacturing to the US. Earlier this year, Apple vowed to start producing the Mac mini in Houston later in 2026. Cook toured the factory this month with officials from the Trump administration, which has made domestic manufacturing a key piece of its agenda. The company had previously assembled the Mac Pro in the US, but that model was discontinued earlier this year.

item.title: 焦点：トランプ氏の北朝鮮接近、揺らぐアジア同盟国の対米信頼感
item.description:
John Geddie Yukiko Toyoda Ben Blanchard Aftab Ahmed
[東京／台北／ニューデリー ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
John Geddie　Yukiko Toyoda　Ben Blanchard　Aftab Ahmed

[東京／台北／ニューデリー ２４日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領が、長年の同盟国である韓国に負担を強いる形で北朝鮮の金正恩総書記に歩み寄る姿勢を示した。これは日本からインドに至るまで、多くのパートナー国が米国はどこまで信頼できるのかを改めて見極めようとしているという、米国にとって安全保障上の重要な局面で起きた出来事だ。

政府関係者や安全保障専門家の話では、トランプ氏が先週、韓国との合同軍事演習の縮小を突然決定して「北朝鮮に対して敵対的だ」と説明したことは、地域の平和を長年支えてきた同盟関係に亀裂が生じるのではないかとの懸念を強めた。

日本では、今後予定される難しい安全保障交渉の中で、自国もトランプ氏の標的になりかねないとの不安が広がっている。台湾は、来月予定されているトランプ氏と中国の習近平国家主席との首脳会談を慎重に見守っているほか、インドでも米国の戦略における自国の位置付けへの確信が揺らぎつつある。

政治リスク分析会社ユーラシア・グループのシニアアナリストで、元米外交官のジェレミー・チャン氏は「今回の（トランプ氏による米韓合同軍事演習縮小の）決定は、米国の安全保障上のコミットメントに対する地域の疑念をさらに強めるだろう」と述べた。

不安材料はそれだけではない。韓国政府は２４日、来月予定されていた別の米韓軍事演習も中止されたと明らかにした。米国側は、イランとの戦争に伴う軍事力の制約を理由に挙げている。

ホワイトハウス高官の１人は、トランプ氏は同盟国がイランとの戦争を十分に支援しなかったことに不満を抱いており、多くの同盟国が自国防衛のためにさらなる負担を負うべきだとの考えを明確にしている、と説明した。

米韓協議に詳しい関係者によると、トランプ氏は北朝鮮との対話再開を強く望んでおり、支持率が低迷するイラン戦争への批判をかわすため、外交分野で成果を上げたいと考えているという。

＜日本で高まる警戒感＞

トランプ氏の金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記への会談呼びかけは、これまでのところ北朝鮮から冷淡な反応しか得られておらず、結果として核保有国である北朝鮮を勢いづかせる恐れがある。

自民党有力議員の１人、小野寺五典元防衛相は２０日のＢＳフジの報道番組で、こうした展開について日本としては「非常に困る」と述べた。トランプ氏の融和姿勢にもかかわらず、北朝鮮は同日、日本海に向けて複数の弾道ミサイルを発射し、韓国と日本で警戒が強まった。

ただ、日本側がより懸念しているのは、在日米軍駐留経費の日本側負担を巡る交渉におけるトランプ氏の対応だ。ある日本政府高官は、トランプ氏が予告なく大幅な負担増を求める可能性があり、それは日本国内で政治的に受け入れがたいものとなりかねないと語った。

複数の専門家は、１０月に予定されている日米共同演習「キーン・ソード」が交渉材料として利用される展開もあり得るとみている。日米両政府の関係者は現時点で演習縮小は予想していないと説明しているが、トランプ氏がいつ方針変更するか分からないと警戒もしている。

キーン・ソードは、米軍の装備や人員がイラン情勢への対応に振り向けられているという面から、２０２４年実施時より規模が縮小されてもおかしくない。実際、米海軍でアジアに前方展開する唯一の原子力空母「ジョージ・ワシントン」が、中東で活動する空母「エーブラハム・リンカーン」支援のため中東へ向かったことは、中国に対する米国の抑止力が弱まるのではないかとの懸念を呼んでいる。

それでも、今月アジアを訪問した米国防総省のコルビー政策担当次官は、日本からフィリピンへ連なる「第１列島線」における戦闘即応態勢の確保は依然として米国の重要課題だと強調した。

＜台湾は米中首脳会談注視＞

中国による軍事的圧力への懸念が最も強いのは台湾だ。トランプ氏は、中国との良好な関係と脆弱な貿易休戦状態を維持するため、総額１４０億ドル規模の台湾向け武器売却計画の承認を保留している。

来月ワシントンで予定される米中首脳会談を前に、台湾当局者らは、米国が少なくとも武器売却案件を小分けにし、中国を過度に刺激しない形で進めるのではないかと予想する。

一方、台湾国防部系シンクタンク「国防安全研究院」の研究者は、トランプ氏の発言と実際の米国の行動には違いがあると指摘。情報共有、軍事訓練、哨戒活動など、台湾に対する米国の支援は依然として相当な規模で続いていると分析している。

実際、米海軍機は２１日に台湾海峡上空を通過。米国はこれについて「自由で開かれたインド太平洋へのコミットメントを示すものだ」と説明している。

＜インドでも信頼に揺らぎ＞

トランプ氏の最近の動きはインドにも衝撃を与えている。複数の安全保障専門家から聞こえてくるのは、米国がロシアと中国への対抗軸として長年進めてきたインドとの関係強化の成果を、自ら損なう恐れがあるとの見方だ。

さらに６月には、米国防総省が「インド太平洋軍司令部」の名称を「太平洋軍司令部」に戻した。これに関して一部の専門家は、インドの戦略的重要性が低下した兆候ではないかと受け止めている。

国防総省はその見方を否定するが、トランプ氏がインド製品に高関税措置を導入したり、インド・パキスタン停戦を仲介したと繰り返し主張したりしていることは、既にインド側の不満を高めていた。

事情に詳しいインド側関係者２人によると、インド政府は現在、米国との長期的な防衛契約に慎重な姿勢を強めているという。

紛争監視団体「武力紛争位置・事象データプロジェクト（ＡＣＬＥＤ）」のシニアアナリスト、パール・パンディア氏は「今回の決定で、トランプ氏の取引重視の外交姿勢が一層裏付けられた。同盟国であっても、個別政策を巡る意見の相違が、二国間関係全体にコストをもたらし得ることを示している」と述べた。

item.title: パキスタン、イランと和平の道筋協議 「大きな進展」と評価
item.description: ［イスラマバード ２５日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［イスラマバード　２５日　ロイター］ - 米イラン交渉の仲介役を務めるパキスタンのナクビ内相は２５日、和平への道筋に焦点を当てた協議で「大きな進展」があったと述べた。同相は、ムニール陸軍元帥とともに２４日にイランの首都テヘランを訪問していた。

パキスタン軍の発表によると、ムニール氏は、イラン側とさらなる事態悪化を防ぐための措置、ホルムズ海峡の再開、紛争の早期終結について協議した。

ナクビ氏は、イラン側と紛争解決に向けた「イスラマバード覚書」の復活を協議したとし、協議で著しい進展があったと述べた。「イランの大統領は自国政府の視点を率直に語り、われわれは関連する問題について非常に建設的な意見交換を行った」とＸに投稿した。

複数のパキスタン筋によると、ムニール氏は先週、トランプ米大統領と電話会談した。会談はトランプ氏からの申し出によるもので、パキスタンの影響力を利用してイランを交渉の席に復帰させることが趣旨だったという。

item.title: New Zealand's main opposition party supports social media ban for under-16s
item.description: Labour, New Zealand's main opposition party, said on Tuesday it would support a ban on social media for under-16s, removing a major obstacle for Prime Minister Christopher Luxon after his coalition partners said they would block the legislation.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Labour, New Zealand's main opposition party, said on Tuesday it would support a ban on social media for under-16s, removing a major obstacle for Prime Minister Christopher Luxon after his coalition partners said they would block the legislation. Luxon on Monday said the [USN:L1N44L039 TEXT:"proposed laws"] would require social media platforms to take reasonable steps to verify users' ages, including by utilising existing account information, facial technology and digital identity documents. Platforms could face fines of up to 10% of global revenue for non-compliance. "With Labour's support there is no reason for the government to delay the bill and we expect to see it in through its first reading before the election," Labour leader Chris Hipkins said in a statement. Luxon's two coalition partners, the New Zealand First party and the ACT Party, said on Tuesday they would not support the bill, raising the possibility it may fail to pass through parliament before an election scheduled for November 7. "We have been concerned with the proposed legislation and the direction and slippery slope that legislation like this will inevitably take our country," New Zealand First leader Winston Peters, who is also the country's foreign minister, said in a post on X. Australia was the first country to ban social media for under-16s and many others, including Britain, are [USN:L6N44L075 TEXT:"taking steps"] to curb access to the platforms for children and younger teenagers.

item.title: Wife of active-duty US Army sergeant is deported
item.description: The wife of a U.S. Army sergeant was deported to Honduras on Monday, marking the latest example of the impact of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown on relatives of members of the U.S. military.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: The wife of a U.S. Army sergeant was deported to Honduras on Monday, marking the latest example of the impact of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown on relatives of members of [USN:L4N44L066 TEXT:"the U.S. military"]. Cristy Maryori Villafranca-Trejo "was removed from the United States" on Monday, a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said in an email. Army Sergeant Hedar Leonel Turcios Juarez told ABC News his wife, the mother of a 6-year-old, was deported to Honduras. Villafranca-Trejo is at least the seventh spouse or parent of an active-duty U.S. military service member to be deported under the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown, according to an Associated Press tally. The Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, which is part of DHS and has been the face of President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown and deportation drive, arrested her on July 11 after conducting what the DHS called a "targeted immigration enforcement operation." The DHS said she received due process. Turcios Juarez previously said ICE officers detained his wife outside a Walmart in July as their daughter watched. He said his wife left Honduras in 2016 due to violent crime in the country. The DHS alleged that she illegally entered the United States. Turcios Juarez joined the military and became a U.S. citizen in 2024 after a nine-month deployment to the Middle East, according to ABC News. He said he began pursuing citizenship for his wife, hoping his service would help expedite her naturalization process. Over the weekend, the immigrant father of a U.S. sailor on board the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier, which was deployed in the Middle East during the Iran war, was taken into federal immigration custody and remains in detention. Trump has pursued an [USN:L4N44L066 TEXT:"immigration crackdown"] that includes revocations of visas and green cards and an aggressive deportation drive. He says the crackdown aims to improve domestic security. Rights groups say the crackdown has violated free speech and due process rights and created an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about [USN:L4N3ZU0AN TEXT:"racial profiling"]. While Trump campaigned in 2024 on a platform of stopping illegal immigration, his administration has also made legal immigration more difficult - for example, by [USN:L6N3XM11V TEXT:"imposing new and expensive fees"] for applicants of certain work visas.

item.title: 片山財務相､強い経済の構築と財政の持続可能性を両立する-27年度予算
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 片山さつき財務相は2027年度の予算編成に関し、歳出改革を進めながら強い経済と財政の持続可能性を両立し、市場の信認を得る考えを示した。25日の閣議後会見で語った。

片山財務相は、高市早苗政権が掲げる責任ある積極財政の下、「強い経済の構築と財政の持続可能性を両立、一体的に実現したい」と説明。市場関係者に「丁寧に説明し、市場からの信認も引き続き確保していく」と語った。

概算要求の規模に関する問いに対しては、今月末の締め切り後に精査すると述べるにとどめた。報道各社によると、27年度予算の概算要求は初めて130兆円を超え、4年連続で過去最大となる見通し。

来年度の概算要求基準においては、危機管理・成長投資のための「新たな投資枠」が新設された。要求上限は設けず、金額を示さない事項要求も可能とする。高市政権は大型補正予算からの脱却へ予算編成の抜本改革を進めるていることからも、当初予算には膨張圧力がかかりやすい。

高市政権が掲げる成長戦略を巡り財政悪化への懸念が根強い中、債券市場では金利上昇が進んできた。18日には新発10年債利回りが一時2.945%と、1996年以来の高水準に達している。

片山財務相は、米国が新たに発動した対イラン制裁について、ホルムズ海峡の一刻も早い開放が必要だと発言。米国とイランの協議が再開し、核問題を含めた最終合意の早期実現が重要との認識を示した。

ベッセント米財務長官は24日、イランの「生命線」としてデジタル資産など5分野を対象に、世界経済から孤立させる「前例のない」取り組みを開始すると発表。イランと取引を続ける国は米国の制裁対象となる恐れがあると警告した。

item.title: Rangers roll up season-high 11 runs in blowout of White Sox
item.description: Corey Seager went 3-for-4 with three RBIs and Jake Burger and Wyatt Langford each homered while collecting two hits and two RBIs, boosting the visiting Texas Rangers to an 11-2 victory against the Chicago White Sox on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Corey Seager went 3-for-4 with three RBIs and Jake Burger and Wyatt Langford each homered while collecting two hits and two RBIs, boosting the visiting Texas Rangers to an 11-2 victory against the Chicago White Sox on Monday. Kumar Rocker pitched effectively into the sixth inning as the Rangers romped past the American League Central-leading White Sox to take a half-game lead on the idle Houston Astros atop the AL West. Texas scored in five of its first six times at bat, providing ample support for Rocker, who picked up his first victory since July 27. Rocker (5-10) spaced two runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings while walking three against eight strikeouts. Tristan Peters reached Rocker for a two-run homer in the bottom of the second to pull the White Sox within 3-2, but the Rangers responded with another crooked number against Chicago right-hander Jose Urquidy. Seager drove in two runs in the third with the first of his two doubles. He added an RBI double against Tyler Schweitzer in the fifth. Burger, who played for Chicago from 2021-23, homered against Schweitzer to lead off the fifth. Langford punctuated the scoring with a two-run blast in the ninth as the Rangers posted a season-high run total. Urquidy (2-2) struggled in his first start since 2023, when he was with Houston. Acquired in a July trade with the Pittsburgh Pirates, he had a stint in the minor leagues, then pitched twice in relief for the White Sox, including six shutout innings Wednesday in a victory against the Chicago Cubs. Texas reached Urquidy early on Monday. He yielded five runs and six hits in three innings with two hit batters, four walks and two strikeouts while throwing 93 pitches. Ezequiel Duran added two hits and two RBIs for Texas. Rangers pitching retired the last 10 White Sox batters after Chase Meidroth's two-out walk in the sixth. Rangers right fielder Brandon Nimmo leaped over the right field wall to rob Andrew Benintendi of a potential game-tying two-run blast to end the Chicago first. Plate umpire Chris Guccione ejected Rangers designated hitter Joc Pederson in the second inning. Pederson continued to argue from the dugout after he was not granted an ABS challenge following a strikeout. By taking the opener of a three-game set, Texas evened the season series with Chicago at two wins apiece. --Field Level Media

item.title: AI chipmaker Enflame sets subscription date for near $900 million Shanghai IPO
item.description: Enflame Technology , one of China's leading AI chipmakers, will open share subscriptions on September 2 for its 6 billion yuan ($892.21 million) IPO on Shanghai's tech-heavy STAR Market, a regulatory filing showed late on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Enflame Technology , one of China's leading AI chipmakers, will open share subscriptions on September 2 for its 6 billion yuan ($892.21 million) IPO on Shanghai's tech-heavy STAR Market, a regulatory filing showed late on Monday. The chipmaker, backed by technology company Tencent Holdings (0700.HK) , will issue 43.04 million new shares, representing a 10% stake in its enlarged share capital of approximately 430 million shares, with preliminary price consultations set to begin on August 28, the filing showed. Of the total offering, an initial 8.61 million shares have been allocated to strategic investors, while 27.54 million and 6.89 million shares have been set aside for institutional and retail tranches, respectively. Founded in 2018, Shanghai-based Enflame is grouped alongside Moore Threads (688795.SS) , MetaX (688802.SS) , and Biren Technology (6082.HK) as one of China's "four little GPU dragons." The other three companies have all gone public over the past year, riding a wave of global enthusiasm for semiconductor companies. Enflame plans to allocate the proceeds to develop and commercialise its fifth- and sixth-generation AI chips, as well as advanced AI software and hardware collaborative innovation projects. China's [USN:L4N42H0N2 TEXT:"onshore technology IPOs"] are on track for their strongest year since 2023 as Beijing seeks to bolster listings of chip and artificial intelligence companies in a push for tech self-reliance amid the country's rivalry with the U.S. But a roughly 45% slump in the shares of Unitree (688836.SS) , China's best-known humanoid robot maker, since a more than fivefold jump on its Shanghai debut has triggered concerns about [USN:L4N44K01K TEXT:"bubble risk"] and whether enthusiasm for AI and robotics has outpaced fundamentals. CITIC Securities is acting as the lead underwriter for Enflame's deal, with Guotai Haitong Securities and GF Securities as joint lead underwriters. ($1 = 6.7249 Chinese yuan renminbi)

item.title: German broker Scalable opens investment platform to major AI chatbots
item.description: The German broker Scalable Capital on Tuesday said its account holders could now use major artificial platforms like ChatGPT and Claude to conduct trades and analyze their portfolios.
item.dc:creator: Tom Sims
item.content:encoded: The German broker Scalable Capital on Tuesday said its account holders could now use major artificial platforms like ChatGPT and Claude to conduct trades and analyze their portfolios. The new service, which Scalable said was a first for a European bank, comes in addition to the app and website as ways to access customer accounts and includes a number of security measures. Scalable founder and Co-CEO Erik Podzuweit said the service is a "first step" ahead of the mass adoption of AI for its customers that is likely to occur after it provides the capability directly within its own app. "A lot of people might still be hesitant to let ChatGPT look at their portfolio, manage their portfolio. So I think that it's a first step," he told Reuters. He also said his hypothesis is that usage of AI will on average result in better returns but that it remains to be seen. Scalable, founded in 2014, has more than 1 million clients with more than €60 billion in assets. It is primarily used in Germany and Austria but also operates in Italy, Spain, France and the Netherlands. New financial firms like Scalable have further increased competition in an already crowded German banking landscape, offering retail investors an easier and cheaper path to investments than at many traditional lenders.

item.title: Autopsy finds cocaine, heroin contributed to Brandon Clarke's death
item.description: Memphis Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke had heroin, cocaine, morphine and multiple prescription drugs in his system when he died, according to the autopsy results released by the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Memphis Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke had heroin, cocaine, morphine and multiple prescription drugs in his system when he died, according to the autopsy results released by the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner on Monday. His death was ruled an accident. The effects of heroin and cocaine were ruled to be the cause of death, with the "combined effects of multiple prescription medications" listed as "other significant conditions." On May 11, Clarke, 29, was discovered unresponsive in a bedroom at a residence in the San Fernando Valley and was pronounced dead at the scene by paramedics. First responders on the scene where Clarke was found reported they saw cannabis products, vape devices, syringes, Narcan and an unidentified "powdery white substance." The autopsy release came more than two weeks after a preliminary announcement from the medical examiner included largely the same information. Clarke played his full seven-year NBA career with the Grizzlies after playing college ball for San Jose State and Gonzaga. Over 309 games (50 starts), he averaged 10.2 points and 5.5 rebounds, and he wound up fourth in Rookie of the Year voting in 2019-20. Last season, he appeared in just two games for Memphis, both starts in December, and he averaged four points and three rebounds. He missed the beginning of the season following a knee operation and the end of the campaign because of a calf injury. --Field Level Media

item.title: 米アップルが「Mac mini」新モデル、約2年ぶりに投入へ
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米アップルはデスクトップパソコン（PC）「Mac mini」の新モデルを約2年ぶりに投入する準備を進めている。事情に詳しい複数の関係者が明らかにした。
新型デスクトップは数日中にも発表される見通しで、次期「iPhone」を披露する9月のイベントに先立つ可能性がある。計画が非公開であることを理由に関係者が匿名で明らかにした。アップルは自社製プロセッサーの「M5」と「M6」の両世代を搭載したモデルをテストしている。
今回の刷新は、現行Mac miniの需要が急増していることを受けたものだ。Mac miniはAIアプリケーションをローカル環境で実行するためのツールとして人気が高まっている。一方、メモリー半導体の不足により、アップルが同製品の在庫を確保することが難しくなっている。
刷新されたMac
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米アップルはデスクトップパソコン（PC）「Mac mini」の新モデルを約2年ぶりに投入する準備を進めている。事情に詳しい複数の関係者が明らかにした。

新型デスクトップは数日中にも発表される見通しで、次期「iPhone」を披露する9月のイベントに先立つ可能性がある。計画が非公開であることを理由に関係者が匿名で明らかにした。アップルは自社製プロセッサーの「M5」と「M6」の両世代を搭載したモデルをテストしている。

今回の刷新は、現行Mac miniの需要が急増していることを受けたものだ。Mac miniはAIアプリケーションをローカル環境で実行するためのツールとして人気が高まっている。一方、メモリー半導体の不足により、アップルが同製品の在庫を確保することが難しくなっている。

刷新されたMac miniは、今年下期に投入される一連の新製品の一つとなる。アップルは今週中にもiPhone発表イベントの招待状を送付する見通しだ。9月9日に開催される可能性が高いイベントでは、同社初の折りたたみ式スマートフォンに加え、「iPhone 18 Pro」シリーズが発表される。

同社はまた、フィットネス機能の強化やSeries 12モデルへのセラミックケースの選択肢追加など、小幅な変更を施した複数の新型スマートウオッチ「Apple Watch」を準備している。早ければ9月の製品発表イベントで新型「AirPods」を披露する計画もある。

関係者によると、新製品にはアップルのエントリーモデルのイヤホンを刷新した「AirPods 5」が含まれる。同モデルが最後に刷新されたのは24年。一方、カメラを搭載したAirPodsは来年まで登場しない見通しだ。

アップルは今年、同社初となる画面付きスマートホーム端末も投入する予定だ。同製品は顔認識を使ってユーザーを識別し、個人に合わせたコンテンツを表示する。新型のセットトップボックス「Apple TV」とスマートスピーカー「HomePod mini」も準備している。

item.title: インドネシア、信頼できる商品取引所構築へ＝監督トップ候補
item.description:
Bernadette Christina Stefanno Sulaiman
[ジャカルタ ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Bernadette Christina　Stefanno Sulaiman

[ジャカルタ ２４日 ロイター] - インドネシアで新たに設立される鉱物・戦略コモディティー取引所について、プラボウォ大統領から監督責任者候補に指名されたサルジト氏は２４日、信頼できるインフラを備えた形で構築されると述べた。

商品取引所は２０２７年１月１日に業務を始める予定で、政府がインドネシア産の商品価格に対する影響力を強化する取り組みの一環となる。インドネシアは一般炭、パーム油、ニッケルの世界最大の輸出国で、すず、銅、ボーキサイト、コーヒー豆の主要な供給国でもある。

サルジト氏は、議会金融委員会が適格性審査のために開いた公聴会で「人々は市場が透明で公正、秩序があり流動性が高いかどうかを常に評価する」とし、「市場に厚みや誠実さがなければ、業界関係者やトレーダーは信頼しない」と語った。

サルジト氏は金融サービス庁出身で、官僚として最高位に当たる消費者保護担当副長官を２０２４年に退任した。就任には議会の承認が必要となる。

item.title: Rupee bolted in place by central bank muscle, traders wince
item.description: Sustained corporate dollar demand ran into likely intervention by the Reserve Bank of India on Tuesday, leaving the Indian rupee trapped in a narrow range and speculative interest muted.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Kalra
item.content:encoded: Sustained corporate dollar demand ran into likely intervention by the Reserve Bank of India on Tuesday, leaving the Indian rupee trapped in a narrow range and speculative interest muted. The rupee was at 95.70 per dollar as of 10:50 a.m., little changed on the day and lumbering in an under-5 paisa range. "There is no room to initiate fresh positions given the tight ranges," a trader at a Mumbai-based bank said. A sizeable rupee jump could attract fresh short positions but that doesn't appear to be on the horizon soon, he added. Persistent interventions by the central bank have sapped the currency's volatility over the last two weeks. "As long as geopolitical tensions persist, the RBI may prefer to use incoming dollars to build reserves and reduce its outstanding forward position rather than allow a sharp appreciation in the rupee," said Amit Pabari, managing director at FX advisory firm CR Forex. The central bank's inflow-boosting measures have garnered nearly $73 billion between June 8 and August 21, helping lift forex reserves to striking distance of their record high. Meanwhile, Indian equities dipped on Tuesday, tracking weakness in regional stocks as investors assessed tensions in the Middle East and the impact on oil supplies. Pakistan and Iran made "[USN:L6N44M071 TEXT:"significant progress"]" in talks that focused on the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and a path to peace, Pakistan's interior minister said on Tuesday, at the end of a visit to Tehran. Iran has also promised to retaliate against expanded U.S. economic sanctions that the Americans said would cut off Iran's economic lifeline. Brent crude oil futures were last a tad higher at $92.3 per barrel. Asian currencies were mostly rangebound while the dollar index drifted higher to 99. U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's debut speech at the annual Jackson Hole conference this week will also be in focus as investors pay attention to his remarks about the recent surge in long-tenor bond yields.

item.title: Indian shares subdued as Middle East tensions persist, Nifty expiry looms
item.description: Indian shares edged lower on Tuesday as higher oil prices due to Middle East tensions weighed, while investors awaited the monthly expiry of Nifty 50 derivatives contracts.
item.dc:creator: Bharath Rajeswaran, Vivek M
item.content:encoded: Indian shares edged lower on Tuesday as higher oil prices due to Middle East tensions weighed, while investors awaited the monthly expiry of Nifty 50 (.NSEI) derivatives contracts. The Nifty fell 0.32% to 24,142.25 and the BSE Sensex (.BSESN) shed 0.24% to 77,184.66 as of 9:58 a.m. IST. Fourteen of the 16 major sectors logged losses. The broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100) and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100) were muted. In the latest escalation of geopolitical tensions, Iran promised to retaliate against expanded U.S. economic sanctions that Washington said would cut off Tehran's economic lifeline. Brent crude futures hovered around $92.5 per barrel. "While the domestic earnings backdrop has improved meaningfully, external factors such as Mideast tensions have raised the risk of elevated crude and renewed supply-chain disruptions, both of which are important macro variables for India," said Bhautik Ambani, CEO of AlphaGrep Mutual Funds. Investors will also focus on the Nifty 50's first monthly derivatives expiry under the new closing auction session for stocks with futures and options contracts tied to them, which has led to [USN:L4N4410GH TEXT:"volatility"] in benchmark indexes during weekly derivatives expiry sessions. "When too little volume sits in the auction book, the equilibrium price can drift away from where continuous trading left off, and that is exactly what unsettled traders in the initial weeks," said Rishabh Nahar, partner and fund manager at Qode Advisors. The effectiveness of CAS will be tested not only during the Nifty 50 monthly expiry later today but also on the day the latest MSCI index rejig takes effect after market close on August 31, two traders said. Among stocks, Great Eastern Shipping (GESC.NS) gained 2% after the company's board said it will consider a share buyback proposal. Hindustan Copper (HCPR.NS) fell 6.5% after the government offered to divest up to a 6% stake in the company at a 10.5% discount to its last close.

item.title: グッゲンハイム、資金調達事業体のローン価格急落－会計処理に疑念
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米資産運用会社グッゲンハイムインベストメンツ傘下の資金調達事業体（特別目的会社）が借り入れたローン（貸付債権）の取引価格が24日、相対のセカンダリー市場で急落した。

グッゲンハイムの親会社グッゲンハイムパートナーズは、米大リーグ・ドジャースの筆頭オーナーで、自身の金融帝国が検察の捜査の渦中にあるマーク・ウォルター氏が最高経営責任者（CEO）を務める。

ブルームバーグ集計データによると、GIHボロワーが調達した11億8000万ドル（約1877億円）相当の第1順位担保権付きローン（2031年満期）は、24日の提示価格が額面1ドル当たり72.5セントと、5セント余り急落した。2024年11月の価格設定以降の安値を更新した。

ウォルター氏傘下の企業が公開市場で取引されていない状況を考えると、ローン取引価格の下落は、同氏のビジネスに捜査が及ぼす潜在的な影響について、投資家の評価を反映する一つの指標と受け止められる。

GIHボロワーの第2四半期の収入は前年同期比38%減少し、利益指標も77％急低下した。 「グッゲンハイム・プライベート・インベストメンツ（GPI）」からのアドバイザリー手数料計上の遅れが主な要因と説明した。GPIの会計処理が内部告発の対象となり、ウォルター氏の金融帝国に対するより広範な捜査および調査に発展した。

グッゲンハイムのアン・ウォルシュ最高投資責任者（CIO）は24日、ブルームバーグテレビジョンとのインタビューで、GPIについて、「監査法人と協議した結果、会計処理は適切だったと考えている」と語った。

グッゲンハイムの担当者にコメントを求めたが、これまでのところ返答はない。

原題：Guggenheim Loan Drops to New 73-Cent Low With Firm in Spotlight（抜粋）

item.title: サッカー＝ＵＥＦＡ会長、ＦＩＦＡ会長選出馬せず 「対立候補現れる」
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - 国際サッカー連盟（ＦＩＦＡ）との対立が深まっている欧州サッカー連盟（ＵＥＦＡ）のアレクサンデル・チェフェリン会長は、現職のＦＩＦＡ会長であるジャンニ・インファンティノ氏の対立候補としてＦＩＦＡ会長選に自身が出馬することはないと明言した。

ＦＩＦＡ主催大会の放映権などを管理する商業法人を設立し、その株式の２０％を民間投資家に売却するというインファンティノ氏の提案は、撤回後もサッカー界を揺るがしている。アジア（ＡＦＣ）や北中米カリブ海（ＣＯＮＣＡＣＡＦ）の各地域連盟の支持を受けたＵＥＦＡはこの提案への反対運動を主導しており、チェフェリン氏はインファンティノ氏が退任すべきだと示唆した。

チェフェリン氏はポッドキャスト番組で「（インファンティノ氏に）選択肢は２つある」と述べ、「一つは、彼が自分には支持がないと悟ることだ。ここで言う支持とは、単に投票権を持つ人々からの政治的な支持だけではない。サッカー界全体、ファン、選手、元選手、そしてコーチらからの支持のことだ」と指摘。さらに「もう一つの選択肢は来年３月の選挙に出馬することだが、その場合は対立候補が現れるだろうと私は考えている。誰になるかはまだ分からないが」と続けた。

一方、インファンティノ氏は世界各地の連盟から厳しい非難を浴びながらも、２０１６年から務めているその職を退く気配を一切見せず。３１年までの再選に向けて資金力に乏しい各国協会への支持拡大を重視しているとみられる。

item.title: Lockerbie bombing trial postponed by US judge days before start
item.description: A federal judge on Monday postponed the trial of the man authorities allege built the bomb that blew New York-bound Pan Am flight 103 out of the sky over Lockerbie, Scotland, killing 270 people in 1988.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Andrew Goudsward
item.content:encoded: A federal judge on Monday postponed the trial of the man authorities allege built the bomb that blew New York-bound Pan Am flight 103 out of the sky over Lockerbie, Scotland, killing 270 people in 1988. Jury selection had been scheduled to begin on Wednesday in the trial of Abu Agila Mohammad Mas'ud Kheir Al-Marimi, a Libyan intelligence operative who prosecutors allege once confessed to his role in the 1988 bombing. In the decision to postpone the trial, U.S. District Judge Dabney Friedrich cited the discovery of new evidence that defense attorneys want to examine. The judge said "the newly discovered evidence, as well as evidence located in other countries" and "the need for the defense to determine how best to defend this case" made her reach the decision. Friedrich did not schedule a new trial date but set a court hearing on September 1 to discuss next steps. Mas'ud, now in his mid-70s, has pleaded not guilty to [USN:L1N33213U TEXT:"two criminal charges"] related to the destruction of the aircraft resulting in death and faces a maximum of life in prison if convicted. The Boeing 747 exploded minutes after takeoff from London on December 21, 1988, killing all 259 people on board, including 190 Americans, and 11 people on the ground in Scotland. The bombing made former Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, whose government accepted responsibility for the attack in 2003, an international pariah. Mas'ud has denied wrongdoing and his lawyers have challenged the credibility of evidence gathered by prosecutors, including Mas'ud's alleged confession to a Libyan police officer in 2012, a year after rebel forces toppled Gaddafi's government. Mas'ud's trial in Washington, D.C. federal court has been delayed by years of legal wrangling over the alleged confession and other issues that have exposed the complexities of a U.S. prosecution over a decades-old attack in Britain with crucial evidence gathered in Libya. Mas'ud, who was arrested in Libya and [USN:S8N2YV03B TEXT:"brought to the U.S."] in 2022, is accused of building a time-delayed bomb that was packed into a suitcase and placed in checked baggage in Malta. The explosive-laden suitcase eventually made its way to London Heathrow Airport, where it was stored in the hold of Pan Am flight 103.

item.title: China robot maker Unitree's post-listing slump sparks bubble fears
item.description: A roughly 45% slump in the shares of Unitree, China's best-known humanoid robot maker, since a more than fivefold jump on its Shanghai debut has triggered concerns about bubble risk, retail investor losses and flaws in the IPO system.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A roughly 45% slump in the shares of Unitree, China's best-known humanoid robot maker, since a more than fivefold jump on its Shanghai debut has triggered concerns about bubble risk, retail investor losses and flaws in the IPO system. The wild swings in Unitree's (688836.SS) valuation - [USN:L1N44G01S TEXT:"soaring"] to $66 billion at one point and later plunging by $30 billion - have led to questions about whether enthusiasm for AI and robotics has outpaced fundamentals. The post-listing selloff in the [USN:L1N4470B7 TEXT:"company"], one of the world's largest producers of quadruped and humanoid robots, has also led to soul-searching over China's listing mechanism, which some analysts say distorts prices. Unitree shares steadied on Tuesday after three consecutive days of decline that took their losses to 45% since their debut last Wednesday. The sharp reversal could become a cautionary tale for other Chinese tech companies looking to take advantage of Beijing's "self-sufficiency" drive and IPO opportunities. It also highlights the challenge authorities face in boosting strategic industries without causing a market frenzy. [USN:L1N44E0DE TEXT:"Unitree's debut"] was expected to set the tone for a slew of domestic rivals preparing to come to market. "Investors were carried away by the technology revolution narrative," said Dong Baozhen, chairman of Beijing-based asset manager Lingtong Shengtai, cautioning that "all bubbles are doomed to burst." Unitree's debut performance is a sign of market froth, rather than prosperity in China's tech sector, which has gained prominence over the past year during the country's intense tech rivalry with the U.S. The blockbuster debut came even as Unitree's first-half profit showed signs of a [USN:L6N42D0C6 TEXT:"downshift"]. The company's robots have drawn attention for running, dancing and performing martial arts, but Unitree has had little success in broader commercial applications. Its debut performance "was not fuelled by a rosy prospect, but a desire by some to pump up the shares so as to dump them later at lofty prices," said Abraham Zhang, chairman of venture capital firm China Europe Capital. Unitree reported adjusted net profit fell 53% to 40 million yuan ($5.95 million) in the first three months of 2026, according to its prospectus. Shares of Unitree, which competes with Tesla (TSLA.O) and Hyundai Motor Group-owned Boston Dynamics, finished up 460% on its debut. That compares with an average first-day gain of 226% for newly listed stocks in China over the past three years. RETAIL FRENZY Loopholes in China's IPO system have allowed major shareholders to cash in and make a fortune, while shifting risks to mom-and-pop investors who get involved in secondary market trades, venture capitalist Zhang said. The general belief in regulatory paternalism, which refers to government moves to protect small investors from financial harm, and the absence of short-sellers mean overpriced listings face no immediate pushback, bankers said. Investors were drawn to the Unitree IPO due to perceived state support, as China vies with the United States for tech supremacy, analysts said. Its fast-tracked listing on Shanghai's tech-focused STAR Market, they said, also signalled government blessing as the board is reserved for hard-tech innovators in China's national strategic industries. IPOs by companies such as Unitree and DRAM memory chipmaker CXMT (688825.SS) were chased in China because "there are not many good companies in China's stock market," said Yuan Yuwei, hedge fund manager at Trinity Synergy Investments. Shares of CXMT soared 466% in their Shanghai debut last month. Due to regulators' tight scrutiny, however, only 21 companies went public in Shanghai during the first seven months of the year, compared with 104 in Hong Kong. Some argue that investors in Chinese robotics should be patient, and take a long-term perspective. "Many robot makers spend a lot on research, but commercial orders are not yet in sight," said Gao Xingkun, fund manager of China Southern Asset Management Co. "It's not fair if you only look at profit," he told an online roadshow, drawing a parallel to the [USN:L1N44H01M TEXT:"early stage"] of development for China's now-booming electric vehicle industry. SMALL INVESTORS WERE BURNT Chinese stock exchanges not only vet listing hopefuls, but also give guidance on IPO pricing, limiting bankers' leeway to respond to feverish demand. Dong said the staggering gap between the IPO price and the debut performance means "either one of them must be wrong," and he believes the latter was mispriced. "Debut performance is the barometer of market mood, and exuberant mood breeds bubbles." Hedge fund manager Yuan said pump-and-dump schemes in new listings in China are possible because of restricted short-selling activities. "An IPO stock worth 10 yuan can open at 100 yuan, before sliding for years. It's a rip-off," he said. A retail investor who lost money on Unitree said in a blog post that he supports Chinese innovation, but "the rapid concentration of wealth cannot be built on the pains of retail investors." Those who won the IPO shares "walked away with smiles," leaving many small investors in tears, said Zhang, the venture capitalist. "The capital drama seen in the Unitree listing is not the first in China, and will not be the last." ($1 = 6.7220 Chinese yuan)

The labour deal is subject to ap
